options.text: Saves your uncommitted changes on a stack and restores a clean working tree
Commits your changes to the current branch
Pushes your changes to the remote

questions.explanation: git stash shelves your uncommitted changes onto a stack and gives you a clean working tree, so you can switch context and reapply them later.

options.text: Merges the entire branch containing that commit
Applies that single commit's changes onto your current branch as a new commit

questions.explanation: cherry-pick copies the changes introduced by one specific commit onto your current branch, creating a new commit with a new hash.

questions.prompt: Which statements about the reflog are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: It records where HEAD and branches have pointed over time
It is local to your machine
It can help you recover a commit after a mistaken reset --hard
It is stored on the remote server

questions.explanation: The reflog is a local log of HEAD/branch movements that enables recovery of unreachable commits. It is never pushed to the remote.

questions.prompt: To reapply the most recent stash and remove it from the stack, run: git stash ____
questions.explanation: git stash pop reapplies the latest stash and drops it from the stack (git stash apply reapplies but keeps it).

questions.prompt: You ran `git reset --hard` and lost a commit you needed. How can you get it back?

options.text: It's impossible; the commit is gone forever
Find its hash in git reflog and restore it (e.g. git reset --hard HEAD@{1})
Run git pull to download it from the remote

questions.explanation: A committed change remains referenced in the reflog even after reset --hard. Locate it in git reflog and reset or branch to that hash to recover it.

questions.prompt: Match each command to what it does.

pairs.right: Copy one commit onto the current branch
Show the history of HEAD moves for recovery
Reapply a stash and drop it

questions.explanation: stash shelves work, cherry-pick copies a commit, reflog aids recovery, and stash pop restores then removes the stash.
